memory_candidates.topic: Pinned Challenge signatures versus Lean's unused-instance linters
memory_candidates.detail: When a plan's `## Lean Challenge Statements` block pins signatures via a namespace-wide `variable` block, Lean's unusedFintypeInType / unusedDecidableInType linters will fire on declarations that do not consume every instance. `omit`-ing them repairs the linter but diverges from the pinned signature, which plan-compliance.md treats as a statement-fidelity defect. The correct route is a commented, scoped `set_option` suppression; FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/Compose.lean carries the house precedent for exactly these two linters.

memory_candidates.topic: Adding a .lean file trips the typst pre-commit counts gate
memory_candidates.detail: git-commit-scoped.sh runs scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --counts-only; adding or editing any file under FormalSystem/ drifts formalsystem-file-count / formalsystem-line-count in typst/generated/status.typ and blocks the commit. The remedy is `scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix` (needs a built library; never runs git add) plus staging the regenerated status.typ with the phase commit -- the established convention in this repo's lean phase commits. Do NOT run `lake exe mk_all --lib FormalSystem` as part of that remedy when a plan deliberately keeps a new module out of the aggregator: FormalSystem.lean imports every module directly, so mk_all would make a full build pull the incomplete module. Its import-count warning is non-fatal and expected in that window.
